clinical_review.procedure: Reviewed independently by a medical expert and by a project author. No knowledge base was accepted until every critical item was approved or explicitly flagged for revision. Review was divided by clinical condition.
medical_expert_checklist: The disease-specific diagnostic framework is clinically appropriate.
All concepts are correctly classified as diagnostic, supportive, etiologic, severity, complication, or exclusion evidence.
Every diagnostic rule, criterion, threshold, unit, timing condition, and population restriction is confirmed.
No unsupported rule was invented, and supportive findings cannot independently confirm the diagnosis.
The what-does-not-count, contradiction, insufficient-evidence, abstention, and referral rules reflect safe clinical practice.
Every clinical item is accurately grounded in the cited sources.
project_author_checklist: All concepts and rules have correct source provenance.
The JSON structure, concept identifiers, rule references, and value types are valid and consistent.
Missing evidence remains unknown and cannot accidentally activate a rule.
The verifier is deterministic and reports the decision, supporting evidence, missing or conflicting evidence, and justification.
Clear positive, unsupported, incomplete, contradictory, and threshold-boundary cases are tested.

all_knowledge_bases: A claim-by-claim audit was introduced. Every diagnostic concept, threshold, and relationship was required to trace to one of the two cited sources. Derived elements, such as language normalization and differential-handling logic, were relabelled as implementation logic rather than guideline facts.

Each concept was assigned one of four states: present, absent, unknown, or conflicting. Missing documentation remains unknown. Diagnostic, supportive, etiologic, severity, complication, and management evidence are stored separately, so that only explicitly diagnostic evidence can activate the verifier.

The four knowledge bases keep different decision structures rather than one shared formula: a two-of-three rule for pancreatitis, integrated clinical and imaging assessment for cholecystitis, CT-supported multi-evidence assessment for diverticulitis, and stepwise risk stratification followed by imaging for appendicitis.

Unsupported or partially supported claims were deleted or rewritten, and explicit cautions were added stating that no official two-of-three rule exists for appendicitis, cholecystitis, or diverticulitis.
appendicitis: Five PROVENANCE_NOTE placeholders were replaced with page-cited evidence.
Alvarado, AIR, AAS, and pediatric scores were retained for risk stratification only and cannot independently confirm appendicitis.
Pediatric thresholds, including CRP at or above 10 mg/L, were linked to the relevant WSES statement and page.

clinical_review.known_limitation: Each condition carries one clinician's assessment, so criterion-level agreement between clinicians is not available. Specialty-matched review by two independent clinicians per condition, with adjudication of disagreement, precedes clinical use.
clinical_review.record_of_review: Supplementary Material, section 4 (expert review and acceptance checklist) and Table S1 (specific improvements introduced during iterative revision).

disease.scope: diagnostic and evidence-stratification KB for suspected acute appendicitis in clinical notes, labs, and imaging reports

sources.title: Diagnosis and treatment of acute appendicitis: 2020 update of the WSES Jerusalem guidelines
sources.notes: Use for recommendations, clinical score role, imaging pathway, pediatric/pregnancy cautions, NOM criteria, timing, and complicated appendicitis pathways.

sources.title: Appendicitis - StatPearls - NCBI Bookshelf
sources.notes: Use for text-to-concept mapping of symptoms/signs and common descriptive imaging/lab findings. Do not override WSES diagnostic pathway recommendations.

scientific_guardrails.rationale: Unlike pancreatitis, WSES appendicitis does not define a 2-of-3 diagnostic rule. Diagnosis is a tailored, stepwise synthesis of clinical presentation, risk score, labs, and imaging.
diagnosis_should_not_be_based_on: Alvarado score alone as a positive confirmatory diagnosis in adults
symptoms and signs alone in pregnancy
must_report_uncertainty_when: labs are absent or normal but symptoms persist
imaging is needed but not available
pregnancy/pediatric pathway applies, or elderly/HIV context affects Alvarado-score reliability

logic: Request or extract inflammatory markers/labs where available.
Compute or approximate clinical risk using validated scores when data allow.
Use clinical scores primarily to exclude low-risk disease and identify intermediate-risk patients needing imaging.
Use imaging after initial risk stratification when indicated.
Do not positively confirm adult acute appendicitis using Alvarado score alone.
Use AIR score or Adult Appendicitis Score as preferred adult clinical predictors when computable.
Use ultrasound/POCUS first-line where appropriate and operator expertise exists; use CT/MRI depending on patient group and pathway.
primary_rule.evidence_grade: multiple recommendations; includes strong recommendations for tailored approach, score use for exclusion, AIR/AAS as predictors, combined clinical+US imaging approach

normal_lab_caution.statement: No laboratory value alone can confirm or exclude acute appendicitis; normal WBC plus normal CRP has high negative predictive value. Persistent or progressive right iliac fossa pain after normal investigations should follow the WSES escalation pathway.

cross-sectional preoperative imaging may be avoided before diagnostic +/- therapeutic laparoscopy

pathway_policy.statement: Routine combination of clinical parameters and ultrasound is recommended to improve diagnostic sensitivity/specificity and reduce CT need.
Intermediate-risk patients benefit from observation and systematic diagnostic imaging.
POCUS by an experienced operator is recommended as the most appropriate first-line diagnostic imaging tool in adults and children if imaging is indicated.
Contrast-enhanced low-dose CT is preferred over standard-dose CT for adolescents and young adults with suspected appendicitis and negative US findings.
In pediatric patients, US is suggested as first-line imaging; second-line imaging depends on availability/expertise; routine CT as first-line is discouraged.
In pregnancy, graded-compression transabdominal US is preferred initially; MRI is suggested after inconclusive US where available.

ct_findings.display: enlarged appendix outer diameter >6 mm to 8/9 mm
surrounding fluid collection/abscess with stranding as a complicated/imaging-context feature

us_findings.caution: Use as imaging support only; do not override persistent clinical concern.

periappendiceal_inflammation: soft tissue inflammation at appendiceal base

normalization_notes.caution: Diameter-only findings are supportive but should be interpreted with other imaging signs and clinical context.

complications.definition_context: complicated disease may include perforation, phlegmon, abscess, gangrene, diffuse peritonitis, sepsis, or severe inflammatory spread; use these as complication-context features, not as a standalone diagnostic rule.

features.meaning: appendicolith is important when considering antibiotic-first non-operative management because WSES recommends NOM discussion only in selected uncomplicated cases without appendicolith and notes increased failure risk when appendicolith is present.

management_context_not_diagnostic.statement: Antibiotic-first non-operative management can be discussed as a safe alternative in selected uncomplicated cases without appendicolith, with counseling about failure/recurrence and misdiagnosis risk.

For complicated appendicitis with periappendicular abscess/phlegmon, non-operative management with antibiotics and drainage where available is reasonable where laparoscopic expertise is not available; laparoscopic treatment is an option in experienced hands.

differential_diagnosis.source_policy: Differential list is included as an LLM guardrail to prevent overcalling appendicitis. Listed alternative diagnoses are source-grounded from StatPearls; distinguishing clues are retained only where explicitly source-supported or labeled as conservative implementation cues.

distinguishing_clues: listed by StatPearls as a differential diagnosis; no specific distinguishing clue provided in the source text
items.agent_action: Consider alternative only as a source-listed differential; do not infer distinguishing features unless present in patient record.
Consider mesenteric adenitis when recent viral infection is documented and appendicitis core evidence is weak.
Flag Crohn/terminal ileitis as a mimic when history or ileal inflammation is documented.

distinguishing_clues: listed by StatPearls as renal colic/kidney stones differential; no specific distinguishing clue provided in the source text
items.agent_action: Consider urinary/stone disease only as a source-listed differential unless patient record provides urinary or imaging evidence.

distinguishing_clues: severe cervical motion tenderness may indicate pelvic inflammatory disease
ectopic pregnancy, tubo-ovarian abscess, ruptured ovarian cyst, ovarian torsion, salpingitis, mittelschmerz, endometriosis, and round ligament syndrome are listed differentials
items.agent_action: In relevant patients, state gynecologic differential and missing pelvic/pregnancy evaluation data as implementation needs, not source-proven appendicitis evidence.

distinguishing_clues: complicated cecal diverticulum and right-sided colitis are listed by StatPearls as differentials; no specific distinguishing clue provided in the source text
items.agent_action: Consider only as source-listed differential unless patient record/imaging directly supports colonic pathology.

differential_diagnosis.notes: Differential diagnoses are source-grounded to StatPearls. Only recent viral infection for mesenteric adenitis, severe cervical motion tenderness for PID, and Crohn history/ileal inflammation for Crohn mimic are explicit distinguishing clues found in the StatPearls text. Other workup cues must be treated as implementation logic or patient-record evidence, not direct source claims.

input_schema.symptoms: list of extracted symptoms with evidence text and negation
input_schema.physical_exam: list of signs with evidence text and negation
input_schema.labs: structured WBC, ANC/neutrophils, CRP, temperature if available
input_schema.imaging: structured US/CT/MRI findings with modality and report text
input_schema.timeline: hours/days from symptom onset if available

decision_algorithm.name: Clinical suspicion extraction
decision_algorithm.logic: Identify compatible symptoms/signs such as migratory RLQ pain, RLQ tenderness, anorexia, nausea/vomiting, fever, peritoneal signs.

decision_algorithm.name: Risk stratification
decision_algorithm.logic: Use AIR/AAS preferentially in adults when available; Alvarado can support exclusion/triage but should not confirm adults alone. In children, scores can help exclude but not diagnose alone.

decision_algorithm.name: Lab support
decision_algorithm.logic: Use WBC with differential/ANC and CRP as inflammatory support; normal markers reduce likelihood but do not alone rule out when symptoms persist.

decision_algorithm.name: Imaging pathway
decision_algorithm.logic: Use clinical+US/POCUS where indicated; use systematic imaging for intermediate risk; use low-dose CT after negative US in adolescents/young adults when indicated; use US then MRI in pregnancy; use US first in children.

decision_algorithm.name: Confirm support level
decision_algorithm.logic: Classify as confirmed/highly likely only when imaging, operative findings, or high-risk clinical context with appropriate pathway support is present. Otherwise output suspected/intermediate/low-risk with missing evidence.

decision_algorithm.name: Complication check
decision_algorithm.logic: Flag abscess, phlegmon, perforation, gangrene, diffuse peritonitis, sepsis, prolonged symptoms, high WBC/CRP, appendicolith, and imaging collections.

abstention_rules: If only nausea/vomiting/fever are present without RLQ pain/tenderness or imaging/lab support, do not confirm appendicitis.
If only Alvarado score is high in an adult and no imaging/clinical pathway support is available, do not state confirmed; state high suspicion.
If pediatric case has only score data without imaging/lab context, do not diagnose based on score alone.
If pregnant case has symptoms/signs only, request/require labs and inflammatory markers and follow imaging pathway.
If imaging is negative but pain is progressive or persistent, do not dismiss; recommend cross-sectional imaging/laparoscopy pathway as applicable.

forbidden_outputs: confirmed appendicitis from Alvarado score alone in adults
ignoring negative imaging or normal labs

evidence_interpretation_layer.purpose: Convert extracted isolated features into conservative diagnostic support patterns for an LLM agent.
global_rules: Do not confirm appendicitis from isolated symptom clusters without RLQ localization, inflammatory support, risk-score context, or imaging.
Prefer output labels: low_risk, intermediate_risk_needs_imaging_or_observation, high_suspicion, imaging_supported, complicated_features_present.
When evidence conflicts, preserve both positive and negative evidence and lower confidence rather than forcing a diagnosis.
Use imaging/operative/pathology evidence as stronger support than symptom-only evidence.

patterns.confirmation_requirement: imaging/pathway support or appropriate high-risk surgical pathway support; symptoms alone are not enough for confirmed label.

patterns.action_for_agent: Do not overcall; recommend/flag systematic imaging or observation pathway per WSES.

patterns.caution: Borderline diameter alone should not be treated as conclusive without other features or clinical compatibility.
WBC/CRP elevation alone is association/support, not automatic proof of complicated disease.
Persistent/progressive right iliac fossa pain after normal tests still needs WSES cross-sectional imaging/laparoscopy pathway consideration.

contradictory_and_uncertainty_layer.purpose: Prevent LLM overdiagnosis by explicitly representing negative, conflicting, or alternative-direction evidence.

contradictory_or_confidence_lowering_fea.meaning: Lowers support for typical appendicitis when repeated exams show no RLQ localization.

Consider gastroenteritis or mesenteric adenitis only as source-listed differentials; recent viral infection specifically supports mesenteric adenitis in StatPearls. Dominant watery diarrhea/viral-syndrome wording is an implementation cue, not a direct diagnostic rule.

Consider renal colic or kidney stones as source-listed differentials when patient-record urinary/stone evidence is present. Specific flank/hematuria/colicky pattern is implementation logic unless documented by the patient record.

Consider StatPearls-listed gynecologic differentials when relevant; severe cervical motion tenderness may indicate PID. Positive pregnancy test/adnexal-mass wording should be treated as implementation/workup logic unless documented in the patient record.
Crohn disease/terminal ileitis can mimic appendicitis.
High negative predictive support, but not absolute exclusion when pain persists/progresses.
Supports lower-risk pathway when symptoms settle.
Do not dismiss; WSES recommends escalation pathway.

required_agent_behavior: Report contradictory evidence in the output.
State what evidence would be needed to move from suspected to imaging_supported or confirmed/highly_likely.
Never hide normal labs or negative imaging; they must be represented as evidence, not silently ignored.

clinical_nlp_context_layer.purpose: Make the KB safer for extraction from clinical notes by tracking negation, temporality, and experiencer. This is implementation logic for NLP safety, not a medical diagnostic claim from WSES/StatPearls.

temporal_interpretation_rules.rule: Pain beginning diffuse/periumbilical then localizing to RLQ is stronger than nonspecific abdominal pain alone.
A subtle early exam should not automatically rule out appendicitis if symptoms are evolving.
Symptoms extending beyond 48 hours can occur in complicated appendicitis; interpret with imaging and systemic signs.
Persistent/progressive right iliac fossa pain after normal investigations should trigger WSES escalation logic.

source_grounded_exclusions.excluded_claim: Appendicitis has an official 2-of-3 diagnostic rule.
source_grounded_exclusions.reason: Not supported by WSES or StatPearls for appendicitis.
source_grounded_exclusions.replacement: Use tailored stepwise risk stratification with clinical scores, labs, and imaging.

source_grounded_exclusions.excluded_claim: Alvarado score alone confirms adult appendicitis.
source_grounded_exclusions.reason: WSES states it is not sufficiently specific for positive confirmation in adults.
source_grounded_exclusions.replacement: Use Alvarado mainly for exclusion/triage; prefer AIR/AAS for adult prediction.

source_grounded_exclusions.excluded_claim: Children can be diagnosed by scores alone.
source_grounded_exclusions.reason: WSES suggests against diagnosis based on clinical scores alone in children.
source_grounded_exclusions.replacement: Use scores plus biomarkers and imaging pathway.

source_grounded_exclusions.excluded_claim: Pregnancy appendicitis can be diagnosed on symptoms/signs only.
source_grounded_exclusions.reason: WSES suggests not making diagnosis in pregnancy on symptoms/signs only.
source_grounded_exclusions.replacement: Require labs/inflammatory markers and US/MRI pathway.

source_audit.summary: Core WSES diagnostic pathway, score policy, pediatric biomarker thresholds, imaging pathway, and StatPearls clinical/lab/imaging language are broadly aligned after corrections. Differential and NLP safety layers are now explicitly source-list-only or implementation logic where direct source support is absent.
cautions: This KB is for research LLM diagnostic support only, not autonomous clinical diagnosis.
Appendicitis has no official 2-of-3 diagnostic rule in the WSES and StatPearls sources.
Alvarado/AIR/AAS/PAS should be used according to WSES score-policy limits, not as universal confirmatory rules.

Differential diagnoses are source-listed from StatPearls, but most distinguishing clues are not fully specified by the source text and must be treated as implementation cues or patient-record evidence.
Clinical NLP negation/temporality/experiencer handling is implementation safety logic, not a medical claim from the clinical sources.

page_level_provenance.source_page: WSES PDF pages 6-7 / diagnostic recommendations table
page_level_provenance.exact_quote_or_source_text_summary: WSES recommends a tailored individualized diagnostic approach, use of clinical scores to exclude AA and identify intermediate-risk patients needing imaging, avoiding adult positive confirmation by Alvarado alone, using AIR/AAS as predictors, and imaging after initial risk stratification.
page_level_provenance.verification_method: Re-verified against the WSES guideline PDF.

page_level_provenance.exact_quote_or_source_text_summary: WSES states WBC count/differential/ANC and CRP are useful in children; CRP ≥10 mg/L and leukocytosis ≥16,000/mL are strong predictive factors.
page_level_provenance.verification_method: Re-verified against the WSES guideline PDF.

page_level_provenance.exact_quote_or_source_text_summary: High-risk patients younger than 40 with AIR 9–12, Alvarado 9–10, and AAS ≥16 may avoid cross-sectional imaging before diagnostic ± therapeutic laparoscopy.
page_level_provenance.verification_method: Re-verified against the WSES guideline PDF.

page_level_provenance.exact_quote_or_source_text_summary: StatPearls supports diffuse/periumbilical pain localizing to RLQ, pain with walking/coughing, anorexia, nausea/vomiting, fever, RLQ exam signs, WBC/CRP caution, WBC >10,000, WBC ≥17,000 association, CT/US/MRI descriptive findings, and Alvarado modified score components.

StatPearls lists Crohn ileitis, mesenteric adenitis, cecal diverticulum, gynecologic causes, gastroenteritis, right-sided colitis, renal colic/kidney stones, testicular torsion and related mimics; only limited distinguishing clues are explicit.
page_level_provenance.verification_method: Differential list retained; unsupported distinguishing clues pruned or relabeled.
